structured_output.summary: Phase 6 (AI Gateway) is a substantial, high-quality delivery: 194 Gateway methods across control, telemetry, runtime, multimodal and public-pricing surfaces, with genuine credential/plane isolation, pre-authentication validation, bounded single-dispatch mutations, explicit opt-in runtime replay, typed SSE terminal policies, and byte-exact multipart contracts. The ledger arithmetic checks out (61+79+54=194, with exactly connectRealtime and provision deferred to Phase 7 via machine-recorded overrides), and docs/checks/phase-06.json records 33 actually-executed checks, all exit_code 0, with source_unchanged true and a source_sha256 equal to the SHA supplied for review. Test evidence is real rather than asserted: the runtime suite drives all 49 JSON/text/binary cases directly from the manifest-pinned frozen TypeScript fixture, and the control suite reads the frozen OpenAPI corpus for its extension responses. Two evidence-binding defects keep this below the 9 threshold. First, the packaged independent fixture bundle crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/gateway-contracts.json (12 exact frozen cases) is provenance-verified by tools/verify_native_fixtures.py and shipped in the consumer archive but is read by no test, while docs/GATEWAY.md presents those 12 cases as independent evidence for the 61-method control/telemetry suite -- that suite actually asserts only against an inline hand-authored GOLDEN constant. This is precisely the "claimed coverage unsupported by tests" pattern the gate exists to catch, and it is a regression from the Phase 5 pattern where the equivalent bundle is include_str!-bound into red_team_contracts.rs. Second, the provenance record for that suite's response specimens is an unverifiable comment: the recorded Zod oracle SHA256 matches nothing in the repository and no check validates it, so 61 of 194 methods rest on specimens that are neither reproducible nor tamper-evident. Both fixes are small. Remaining findings are polish: no gateway example alongside the five existing family examples, one unexplained response-assertion exemption, phase-status scope_evidence omitting the three new mapping fragments, and a phase gate whose command set is unchanged from Phase 5.

findings.description: The 12 exact frozen Gateway fixture cases in this bundle are provenance-verified by tools/verify_native_fixtures.py (REQUIRED set at tools/verify_native_fixtures.py:11) and are shipped in the published crate archive via the Cargo include = ["src/**"] rule, but no Rust source or test references the file. A repository-wide grep for 'gateway-contracts' matches only tools/verify_native_fixtures.py and recorded check/review JSON; crates/ has zero matches. By contrast the Phase 5 analogue is bound at crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:27 via include_str!. docs/GATEWAY.md:107 presents these 12 cases under the 'Independent evidence' heading for the 61-method control/telemetry suite, but crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_contracts.rs asserts solely against the inline hand-authored GOLDEN constant declared at line 1088 and contains no include_str! at all. The verification therefore proves the bundle is an exact frozen copy while proving nothing about the test expectations, so the stated independent-fixture coverage for those cases is unsupported by any executed test.
findings.required_fix: Bind the bundle to the suite: add const FIXTURES: &str = include_str!("../src/fixtures/gateway-contracts.json"); to crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_contracts.rs and assert the log_exports.* and rate_limits.* GOLDEN route/response expectations against the corresponding frozen cases (matching on case["call"]["className"]/["member"] as gateway_control_contracts.rs:349-355 already does), failing if any of the 12 cases is unused. Alternatively delete the unused bundle, drop it from tools/verify_native_fixtures.py:11, and remove the claim from docs/GATEWAY.md:107-109.

findings.description: The provenance record for the 61-method suite's response specimens is the bare comment '// Zod oracle source SHA256: 0c546710f5a36070912fce5abcb3a5320adecd60b6ecb9c2e0105a44ddf33b4d'. That digest appears nowhere else in the repository and no tool verifies it, so the specimens behind the GOLDEN constant are neither reproducible nor tamper-evident. docs/GATEWAY.md:109-110 nonetheless states the specimens 'were produced by actual frozen Zod execution, with their oracle source hash recorded in the test file', presenting an unverifiable comment as provenance. This is inconsistent with the governance model established in Phase 1 (manifest-pinned, hash-verified, tamper-rejecting extraction) and with the sibling Gateway suites, which include_str! the manifest-pinned frozen corpus at crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_runtime_contracts.rs:25-27 and crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_control_contracts.rs:345-347. Risk is partially mitigated because route, query-order, header and request-body expectations are literal source-derived values independent of the specimens, and typed model acceptance is independently exercised by the recorded tools/generate_models.py --verify-fixtures run over 27,216 typed cases.
findings.required_fix: Commit the Zod oracle generator and/or its emitted specimen file under contracts/, register it in contracts/manifest.json with its sha256, and verify that hash in tools/verify-contracts.py so the binding is machine-checked; or, if the oracle cannot be committed, replace the comment and the docs/GATEWAY.md:109-110 claim with an accurate statement that these specimens are hand-authored source-derived fixtures.

findings.description: The Phase 6 scope_evidence array lists docs/GATEWAY.md, docs/GATEWAY_CONTROL.md, docs/GATEWAY_RUNTIME.md, docs/STREAMING.md, docs/VALIDATION.md and contracts/native-operations.json, but omits the three new operation-mapping fragments this phase introduced: contracts/native-operation-mappings/gateway.json, gateway-control.json and gateway-runtime.json. Phase 4 (lines 201-206) and Phase 5 (lines 271-274) both enumerate their mapping fragments, so the bookkeeping for the phase that owns the largest mapping set is less complete than its predecessors.
findings.required_fix: Add the three contracts/native-operation-mappings/gateway*.json paths to the Phase 6 scope_evidence array in docs/phase-status.json to match the Phase 4 and Phase 5 convention.

findings.description: There is no Gateway example. The examples directory contains foundation.rs, scan.rs, pagination.rs, management.rs and model_and_red_team.rs, and the recorded scripts/check-package.py output in docs/checks/phase-06.json:611 confirms exactly those five ship in the consumer archive. Every prior family-delivering phase added a compiled example; the largest family in the SDK (194 methods, three distinct credential planes) ships none, so no compiled artifact demonstrates AIGatewayClient::new, with_runtime, or the pricing client wiring that docs/GATEWAY.md:16-28 describes only in prose.
findings.required_fix: Add crates/scm-sdk/examples/gateway.rs behind the gateway feature, demonstrating AIGatewayClient::new with explicit data/admin/IAM endpoints, with_runtime attachment of a separately constructed RuntimeClient, and the standalone AIGatewayModelPricingClient, so the three credential planes are exercised by a compiled artifact under cargo check --all-targets.

findings.description: Inside the 49-case frozen-fixture sweep, 'if method != "deleteResponse" { assert_eq!(result, expected, "{method}"); }' silently exempts one method from the response assertion with no inline justification. The reason is presumably that delete_response returns (), as stated in docs/GATEWAY_RUNTIME.md:30, but an unexplained assertion exemption inside an otherwise exhaustive sweep is easy to widen accidentally during later maintenance.
findings.required_fix: Add a one-line comment stating that deleteResponse returns () so its frozen responseBody is intentionally not compared, and assert the unit contract explicitly (for example assert_eq!(result, Value::Null)) so the method is still positively checked rather than skipped.

findings.description: commands_for(6) returns commands_for(5) with phase-05-rust- report paths rewritten to phase-06-rust- and --require-through-phase bumped to 6; it adds no new command. Phase 6 introduced a new independent fixture bundle, three new mapping fragments and three new integration suites, yet the gate acquires no phase-specific check for them. The new Rust suites are executed only incidentally through cargo test --workspace inside scripts/check-rust.py, and tools/verify_native_fixtures.py globs the fixtures directory, so a bundle can pass the gate while being entirely unused by tests -- which is exactly what happened for gateway-contracts.json. The 33 recorded checks in docs/checks/phase-06.json do match this command set, so the report itself is consistent.
findings.required_fix: Extend verify_native_fixtures.py (or add a phase-6 command in tools/check_phase.py) to assert that every bundle under crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures is referenced by at least one test source, so an orphaned provenance-verified fixture fails the gate rather than passing it.
